A domestic biblical morality on appetite vs. foresight. A biblical-interlude rarity; seldom revived since the Tudors.

title: The Most Virtuous and Godly Susanna
name: The Most Virtuous and Godly Susanna
description: The Most Virtuous and Godly Susanna (c. 1569, Anonymous; England). Susanna resists the lustful Elders, is falsely accused, and is saved by Daniel's cross-examination - staged as a morality of chastity beset by Lechery and False Witness, with Justice as the presiding virtue. A chastity-play rarity; its Daniel trial scene is a miniature courtroom drama.

title: Liberality and Prodigality
name: Liberality and Prodigality
description: Liberality and Prodigality (c. 1567, Anonymous; England). A prince must choose between Liberality (generosity rightly ordered) and Prodigality (wasteful excess), advised by Virtue and tempted by Vice. Performed before Elizabeth, it counsels royal generosity with princely prudence. A court rarity; its counsel-to-princes frame is pure Tudor mirrors-for-magistrates.
